Maria had always been a rising star at her firm, known for her reliability and innovative ideas. When her manager announced a promotion to lead a critical project, Maria was thrilled—until he abruptly revoked the offer, stating, "You’ll be too distracted by your baby’s appointments to handle this role." The comment hung in the air, a blunt reminder of the workplace bias she’d long endured. Maria’s frustration simmered; her pregnancy was a personal matter, not a barrier to leadership. Yet, the rejection lingered, a painful testament to how deeply systemic prejudices still permeate professional spaces.
